summary: Wrote a 2-phase, markdown-only implementation plan at specs/428_enforce_planner_agent_terminal_write/plans/01_terminal-write-enforcement-scope.md (1.5h, waves [1],[2]). Research established that both fix locations this task names are already correct and already closed, and that the one open gap is structural: no .postflight-pending marker is ever armed on skill-orchestrate's direct-dispatch path, so the codebase's only SubagentStop-level block cannot fire there. That claim was independently re-verified by grep during planning (zero matches in skill-orchestrate/ and orchestrate-cycle-*.sh). The plan closes the task by documenting that enforcement scope boundary in three existing source-store files -- handoff-schema.md (primary statement, sited in Outcome Channels rather than Postflight Boundary), skill-lifecycle.md and system-defect-discrimination.md (one-sentence pointers) -- and touches no contract, no detector, no test, and not the handoff-staleness gate.

artifacts.summary: Two-phase plan documenting the terminal-write enforcement scope boundary across three existing source-store markdown files.

decisions_made: Do not edit agents/planner-agent.md: its terminal-write contract is already complete (Stage 0, 6b, 6c, Error Handling, MUST-DO 1/2/7/9) and the failure mode is execution-time interruption, not textual omission.
Do not touch orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh, orchestrate-recover-outcome.sh, the handoff-staleness gate, or task 426's existing test fixtures.

Site the primary statement in handoff-schema.md's '## Outcome Channels' rather than '## Postflight Boundary' (research's suggestion): Outcome Channels already owns the fail-closed return-meta recovery rules and names in_progress by value, so the boundary statement belongs beside the mechanism it qualifies.
Scope the prevention mechanism (marker wiring + SubagentStop terminal-status check) out of this task; surfaced as a non-blocking user_decision instead.

No redeploy phase: the deployed tree is already stale for core/lean/literature and three sibling tasks are editing the same source store this cycle, so a whole-tree regeneration here would deploy their in-flight work. No __WHOLE_TREE__ claim is declared.

user_decision.question: Research found that both fix locations this task names (planner-agent's terminal-write contract and postflight's detection) are already correct and already closed; the only remaining gap is structural -- nothing on the /orchestrate direct-dispatch path can PREVENT a missing terminal write, because no .postflight-pending marker is ever armed for that path. This plan documents that boundary. Should genuine prevention also be funded as a separate follow-up task?
options: Document the scope boundary only (this plan) -- detection via RECOVERY_DECLINED stays the sole enforcement, no new infrastructure
Also scope a separate follow-up task to arm a dispatch-scoped marker in skill-orchestrate and add a SubagentStop-level terminal-status check
user_decision.recommended: Document the scope boundary only (this plan) -- detection via RECOVERY_DECLINED stays the sole enforcement, no new infrastructure
